what_happened: Job 20261103-161454-nmrx ("Judge candidate-shaped PR heads as pending in pr-head and history checks", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. In round 1 of 3 the critic rejected the reading. The reading defines a candidate-shaped head as governed work plus the job's candidate record. The real early pull-request head is the candidate commit built in run/candidate.rs. That commit holds the base tree plus the producer's changes only, with no records. The candidate record is written afterwards and points at the commit by sha, so it cannot be inside it. The planned detector (pending_candidate, which needs candidate.json in the commit) would never match a real early head, and the first CI run would still fail with exit 2. Findings: one blocker (the detector needs a record the real head never contains), two majors (the plan asked the user a question the code answers, and the test fixtures build a fictional head so tests pass while real CI fails), and one minor (matching on violation message text is fragile). No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing makes the reading, at acceptance, trace the object a new rule must recognise back to the code that creates it. Here that is the early-PR flow, which pushes the candidate commit before the candidate record exists. The reading took the shape from the request's wording, and the plan and fixtures then built on it. Test helpers that hand-build the head make the demonstrations pass whatever the real shape is, so the plan's own tests cannot expose the gap. The question was left to the user although reading the code answers it. Planning has three fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan, and a reading defect forces a reject that sends the job back to reading, so all planning spend is lost.
prevention: When a request changes how a check judges an artifact produced by another Athena flow (a PR head, a commit, a record), require the reading to name the producing function and quote the shape it emits. Add a code check that every criterion fixture for such a rule is built by that real producer, or by a helper the producer shares, and not by a hand-built tree. Have the reader reject a reading whose recognised shape cannot be produced by that flow. Do not let the plan leave such a question open for the user when it can be answered from the code.
proposed_request: Make the pr-head and history checks treat the early pull-request head as pending, so the first CI run no longer fails with exit 2. Outcome: when a job opens its early PR, the first CI run on that head passes the pr-head and history checks as pending, and the full landing is still judged in full once the job's records are added. Start from the real head shape: open_early_pr pushes the candidate commit built in crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs, which is the base tree plus the producer's changes and has no records/ entries. The candidate record is written after the push and names the commit by sha, so it is not in the tree. Identify a pending head without needing a record in the head's tree. For example, match the head sha against the candidate commit sha that the job's candidate record names, and state in the reading where CI can read that record (or use another signal that the early-PR flow really produces). Acceptance: (1) a test builds the head with the real early-PR commit builder, or a helper shared with it, and shows check_pr_head and the history check judge it as pending, not as a failure; (2) a head with the same governed changes that is not a known candidate commit is still judged as before; (3) the landing of the same job is judged in full, with a negative test for a pending shape reaching landing; (4) no gate violation is demoted by matching on its message text, so the change is made in the gate rule itself; (5) the CHANGELOG notes the change.
